key_insight: In multi-tenant quantum cloud devices, privacy is governed by coherence and state distinguishability, not just the average gate error rate.
engineering_relevance: Cloud quantum providers should report information leakage alongside standard error metrics so users can assess cross-tenant privacy and security risk before deployment.
method: Defined an information-theoretic leakage metric based on how distinguishable a tenant’s quantum state is to another tenant.
Evaluated leakage on commercial IBM Kingston (156-qubit) and IQM Garnet (20-qubit) hardware.
Tested uniform Pauli randomization over the victim’s register as a defense to suppress leakage.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on two commercial devices showing that boundaries with similar benchmarked error can still exhibit very different leakage, and that the defense reduces leakage in theory but not perfectly in practice due to accumulated errors.
watch_item: Uniform Pauli randomization is theoretically cost-free, but real hardware introduces extra errors that can degrade fidelity and limit the defense’s effectiveness.
paper_title: Coherence Rather Than Error Rate Governs Privacy in Multi-Tenant Quantum Computing
